content:
Last week a few folks gathered at the American Institute of Mathematics for a workshop on Open-source cyberinfrastructure supporting mathematics research. One of the outcomes of the workshop was the apparent need for community infrastructure that can help mathematicians involved in the various projects related to formalization ( :wave:), datasets, computational software, etc., connect with each other.

To that end, we spun up https://code4math.org and a Zulip at https://code4math.zulipchat.com/. Lean folks are very welcome to join those conversations.

Additionally, there are two existing events at the JMM next month that are aligned with our mission: a GitHub for Mathematicians minicourse (including a very quick crash course in running Mathematics for Lean in a Codespace) for any of your colleagues who that might be of interest to. And everyone here is invited to join our reception for mathematics software developers on Thursday, made possible through collaboration with the PROSE Consortium for open source STEM education software and a community grant from the United States Research Software Engineering Association.
